Hi Marta — thanks for the clear ask. I put together a concise responsibilities summary below and attached a short PDF that maps common SIG control families to party responsibilities per mode. Attachment: redwood_sig_mode_mapping.pdf

High-level summary (short answers):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood is responsible for infrastructure, runtime, kernel/OS patching, physical security and network boundary. Customer is responsible for application-level controls (API keys, prompt/content, customer-side encryption keys if BYOK used) and their own identity policies.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Redwood operates the dedicated GPU pool and manages the host infrastructure and OS patching; network boundaries can be customer-isolated — for Dedicated we share responsibility for network controls depending on the chosen network layout (colocated VPC peering vs private link). Customer responsibility increases for tenant-level isolation/config and any customer-managed ingress rules.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer owns the network, physical access (for on-prem), and underlying virtualization; Redwood provides a packaged control plane and the inference runtime as software. Where Redwood runs managed components in the customer VPC, the customer controls network ACLs and subnets; Redwood provides guidance and artifacts for secure deployment.

Quick table (text version):
Control family | Hosted | Dedicated | Private (VPC/on-prem)
Network boundary & firewall | Redwood (edge + NLB) | Shared (Redwood-managed edge; customer-configurable tenant rules) | Customer
Physical access & data center | Redwood (cloud provider DC) | Redwood (cloud provider DC or co-located depending on config) | Customer (on-prem)
OS/host patching | Redwood | Redwood | Customer (unless contracted otherwise)
Encryption at rest | Redwood-managed (default) or Customer BYOK | Same as Hosted with BYOK option | Customer-managed (KMS in VPC or HSM on-prem)
Key management | Redwood KMS integrations (customer BYOK supported) | Customer BYOK recommended | Customer KMS/HSM (recommended)
Logging & audit | Redwood (platform logs) + optional tenant logs | Redwood + tenant logs | Customer (local logs) + Redwood component logs if installed

Notes and caveats: this is intentionally abbreviated. The attached PDF contains the same table plus references to artifacts and the exact SIG question IDs (we annotated each question).

Short answer: when Hosted BYOK is enabled the customer's key material is bound to their account and keystore instance — keys are not stored in a shared plaintext store. We integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) using envelope encryption and per-tenant key references. The attached CSV lists supported providers and notes whether a dedicated keyspace is used or a permissions-based segregation model applies.

If Globex wants a dedicated keyspace and a contractual requirement for HSM-backed keys, we can put that in the Private deployment or in a Dedicated contract with explicit key handling terms. Happy to set up a KMS deep-dive with our infra engineer if you want exact API flows.

Jonas
